title: Index and audit: UT3/D8 central-commutator register bounds (no new kappa)
body:
## What this adds

**Navigation and audit note. No new bound, no kappa change, no PR disposition.** On main, `research/bit-dihedral-commutator` still lists "Does a restored third dirty register help for the same D8 central target?" as open. Open PRs have answered it three times, under two names for the same group (D8 = UT3(F2)):

- #1478 (juper997, `b30fdba4`): r = 2, 3 by census.
- #1573 (steph4n-gh, `0b8c5a69`): every k and every r >= k, by a written proof.
- #1742 (1337isnot1337, `679f3624`): r = 3 again. It was opened about five hours after #1573, cites neither PR, and its DONE note calls four-register models open.

The package `research/ut3-central-commutator-index/` contains:

1. **A family index.** It lists exact heads, scopes and methods for #1443 (on main), #1478, #1573, Discussion 1569 / #1589, #1607 and #1742, with D8/UT3 search aliases so overlap searches find it from either name.
2. **An audit of #1573's proof**, which #1589, #1607, #1662, #1680 and #1690 credit as their all-register premise. I checked normalization, both representations, the span inclusions and the rank-nullity step, and found no gap. Two remarks: the proof never uses `v^T u = 1` (which is why #1589's nilpotent extension works), and since `([g]+1)^2 = 0`, a rank-s coupling is s same-label rank-one calls.
3. **A binding census, written separately** from the group's 3x3 matrices, sharing no code with the audited PRs. The radius-3 balls have 565 states at r = 2 (matching #1478) and layers 1, 56, 1750, 45424 = 47,231 states at r = 3 (matching both #1478 and #1742). The k = 2 meet is empty. An opt-in `--r4` run gives 3,676,891 states and an empty meet at r = 4, a direct check of the case #1742 called open.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -B research/ut3-central-commutator-index/verify.py         # ~13 s -> PASS_UT3_CENTRAL_COMMUTATOR_INDEX
python3 -I -B research/ut3-central-commutator-index/verify.py --r4    # ~42 s, 1.3 GB peak
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/ut3-central-commutator-index
```

The default run passed on Python 3.10 and 3.12, and `--r4` on 3.14. The registered replay and `--check-only` pass, and `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes (42 tests). The controls are:

- The plain coordinate swap is rejected as a homomorphism.
- A prediction with the factor order reversed is rejected.
- A one-target endpoint must give a nonempty meet, and it does at every r.
- The direct eight-call word is accepted and all eight one-call deletions are rejected.
- The verifier fails if the indexed open question disappears from the pinned source README.

## Scope and limits

The unbounded statement rests on #1573's written proof, which I checked by reading. The finite checks corroborate its identities and small cases; they do not replace it. This is not a proof-assistant check or an independent human review. #1742's search remains a valid corroborating replay. Whether to merge, close or relabel any PR is the maintainers' decision. The neighbors (UT4 #1662/#1680/#1690, #1763, #1567) are listed but not audited.

Task: chooser seed `b5f4baff48ffbec78040afb8350266c2` drew bit-mechanisms (`bit-new-register-model`). The scope is declared `changed` to a family index and audit (the consolidation track's scope-navigation pattern) because the drawn cards are saturated. Base `0b1cccf8`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1738#discussioncomment-18921150. A final overlap refresh (2026-10-14 10:07 UTC, complete pagination, 457 open PRs and 430 discussions) found no other index of this family.

## Open next question

The workspace-only route is closed for these targets. The remaining variation is #1573's own: a priced `c = abab` call. The first step is to price one concrete implementation before any search.

## Credit

The results and proofs belong to woklerx (#1443), juper997 (#1478), steph4n-gh (#1573), Arham Tahir (Discussion 1569, #1589), bbMisk (#1607) and 1337isnot1337 (#1742). The lineage includes eumemic (#288), Ali Romman (#468), David Govea (#720), Gareth Davidson (#1333) and commdata2338 (#1414). This PR was prepared for Josie Elliston (@JosieElliston) with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance, in session 20 of a donated overnight run. Apache-2.0.

Workflow feedback: the D8 vs UT3 naming split is a repeatable source of duplicate work. The overlap helper searches top-level READMEs, so an alias line in one indexed README is a cheap fix.
